messages:
Priya (VP Infra): thanks everyone for coming — quick follow-up from the infra portion: posting a short Q&A thread for the regional GPU buffer / autoscale items we promised to clarify. ask here and we'll answer live / asynchronously.

Tom (Platform): thanks! first q — when you said 'edge buffers' in APAC, do you mean reserved nodes sitting idle or just fast reprovisioning from other zones?

Priya (VP Infra): good q. by 'edge buffer' we meant a small warm pool in-region (reserved capacity) + fast fallback to nearby region. reserved pool size is small (single-digit nodes per zone initially) to keep cost predictable.

Rosa (SRE): what are the SLO tradeoffs if the regional pool is empty and we fallback to neighboring region? latency increase numbers?

Priya (VP Infra): expected median latency adds ~45-120ms for cross-region routing (depends on customer region). for certain latency-sensitive enterprise customers we plan to pin to dedicated capacity instead of doing cross-region fallthrough.

Luca (Eng): can you share the autoscaler ramp config you mentioned? approximate ramp steps / cool-downs?

Arjun (Capacity): here's the v0 config we demoed in the talk — note it's conservative and will be tuned after a few weeks of telemetry:
```
min_pool_per_zone: 2
burst_threshold: 0.85
scale_step: 2
cooldown_secs: 180
max_pool_per_zone: 12
region_fallback_order: [ap-southeast-1, ap-northeast-1, us-west-2]
```

Tom (Platform): thanks Arjun. curious how KV cache warmup interacts with fast scale-up — will cold KV loads cause big first-request latency spikes?

Arjun (Capacity): yes, cold KV can add overhead. we're pairing fast warm pools with prefix cache priming for top-10 customer prompts to reduce first-request pain. priming jobs will run as part of pool scale-up.

Rosa (SRE): are we doing any cost simulation for keeping those warm pools year-round vs pure on-demand? want numbers for the finance sync.

Priya (VP Infra): good call. finance asked for a 3x scenario comparison — we have a draft spreadsheet. i'm adding @Tom to own pulling the final numbers by Friday.

Tom (Platform): ack, i'll pull the numbers and post. also can we get a short blurb for the docs about which models are eligible for region-buffering (some quantized variants behave differently)?

Priya (VP Infra): yes — short answer: models that rely on custom kernels + large scratch memory are excluded from the small warm pools until we validate stable startup times. we'll publish a full list in the model-catalog docs.

Luca (Eng): any procurement timeline for new GPU SKUs? people asked about H100 availability and whether it lands in our Dedicated offering this quarter.

Arjun (Capacity): procurement ETA: initial H100 capacity in our cloud partners scheduled for next quarter; Dedicated customers can opt-in for H100 pools once we complete the safety/telemetry checks (~4 weeks after arrival).

Rosa (SRE): followup — if H100 arrives, will autoscaler step sizes change (more capacity per node)?

Priya (VP Infra): yes, autoscaler profiles will get per-hardware tuning. we already plan different scale_step and max_pool_per_zone for H100 vs A100. we'll surface the recommended profile in the Console.

Tom (Platform): small ops question: for A/B rollback during rollouts, is the fallback to the previous model version immediate or queued? want to document for runbooks.

Priya (VP Infra): rollbacks are immediate for safety-critical failures (error rate spike > 5% or latency > 2x SLA). for soft regressions we do canary -> monitor -> roll forward/rollback as a controlled operation. we'll add concrete thresholds to the runbook.

Luca (Eng): ping on the canary thresholds — we briefly mentioned 15 minutes in the all-hands. can we get the exact metrics we monitor (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, cost per 1k tokens)?

Priya (VP Infra): will post the metric set tomorrow. the short list: p50/p95 latency, request error rate, token cost delta vs baseline, user-defined correctness regressions (via evals), and queue depth.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled job: "priming-job/apac-buffer-priming" started (job-id: jb-2026-09-01-0910).

Rosa (SRE): thanks — i noticed priming jobs show up as short spikes in GPU usage in the dashboard. can we throttle them so they don't trigger scale-outs?

Arjun (Capacity): good catch. we'll add a soft cap and tag priming traffic so autoscaler ignores it up to a limit.

Priya (VP Infra): action items from thread: 1) Tom to produce finance comparison (warm vs on-demand) by Fri. 2) Priya to publish model eligibility doc and canary metric list by tomorrow. 3) Arjun to add priming tag to autoscaler ignore list. 4) Infra team to prepare H100 profile draft after arrival. i'll consolidate these into the all-hands notes.

Tom (Platform): i'll drop the spreadsheet link here when ready: https://redwood.company/sheets/gpu-warm-pools (will make editable for infra/finance).

Luca (Eng): thanks Priya and team, helpful thread. :thumbsup:

Priya (VP Infra): thanks everyone — if you have tiny follow-ups drop them here, for larger asks open a ticket in #eng-oncall or create an RFC. will close the thread after all actions are assigned.
